title: Optimize CPU request path: reduce serialization overhead, NUMA-aware thread pinning, and thread-pool improvements
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Reduce CPU-side request-path overhead by optimizing serialization, introducing a NUMA-aware pinned thread pool, and reducing KV cache contention. Improves throughput and lowers p99 tail latency for small/medium requests.
description: Motivation: production traces and microbenchmarks showed significant CPU-side overhead in the request path for small/medium requests (short sequences) caused by (1) expensive JSON serialization on hot paths, (2) thread pool scheduling jitter and cross-NUMA migrations, and (3) KV cache lock contention under high QPS. This PR refactors the request serializer to a compact binary representation on the hot path, introduces a NUMA-aware pinned thread pool for inference request processing, reduces unnecessary wakeups in the existing shared thread pool, and replaces a coarse-grained mutex in the KV cache with a sharded fine-grained lock and lock-free fast-path for cache hits. Changes are split into focused commits for easier review. Checklist: - [x] microbenchmarks (latency and throughput) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] canary deploy in perf-canary cluster - [x] docs/notes for ops on NUMA tuning - [x] load test with dedicated pools Summary of impact: - End-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency improvements for short requests: ~8%/15%/22% respectively in our perf-canary with default batching settings. - CPU user-time for request handling reduced by ~35% on our 16-vCPU service worker instances in the synthetic small-seq load. - Throughput (steady-state QPS) up ~20% when under high concurrency with continuous batching enabled. - KV cache contention reduced 10-15% (contention events measured) enabling higher tail stability under bursty traffic. Related work: follows on previous KV cache fixes (ENG-1742) and continuous-batching perf work (ENG-1903). Risk and mitigation: NUMA pinning is opt-in via a new runtime config flag (cpu.numa_pinning=true) and falls back to the existing scheduler when disabled. Binary serialization is only used on the local in-memory request path and we keep JSON as the external API contract. Deployment plan: canary -> staged rollout with traffic shaping and telemetry dashboards to monitor latency, CPU, and KV cache contention.
commits: Refactor hot-path serializer to compact binary format and fast-path for common message shapes
Add NUMA-aware pinned thread pool implementation and config toggles
Introduce pinned-worker scheduler to reduce cross-socket migrations and wakeups
Replace kv_cache coarse mutex with sharded locks and lock-free fast-path for hits
Add unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end perf harnessing scripts
Update ops docs and add tuning guide for cpu.numa_pinning
review_conversation: Maya Reddy: Nice separation of concerns. Can you quantify serializer allocs?
Asha Patel: Serializer fast-path avoids heap alloc for typical payloads; microbench shows 0-2 allocs per request vs 5-7 before.
Jae Kim: NUMA pinning may cause degraded throughput on oversubscribed nodes; please gate behind toggle and document.
Asha Patel: Agreed; added cpu.numa_pinning flag and fallback to existing pool. Added ops doc with guidance.
Oliver Grant: KV cache sharding looks good but please add a perf test for worst-case contention scenarios.
Asha Patel: Added contention stress test in bench/perf_canary and included results in PR description.
ci_checks: benchmarks: fail on first run (regression for long-seq workload) -> adjusted batch heuristics and rerun
notes_for_ops: cpu.numa_pinning is disabled by default. To enable, set cpu.numa_pinning=true in the runtime config and pin service workers per the ops guide. Recommended for single-tenant or dedicated pools where vCPU placement is controlled. Monitor request_path_latency, worker_cpu_user_seconds, and kv_cache_contention metrics after rollout.
performance_summary: Perf-canary (c5-16x equivalent nodes): small-seq synthetic workload (seq_len=32, tokens/sec focused): p50 -8%, p95 -15%, p99 -22%, CPU user-time -35%, throughput +20%. Long-seq regression fixed by adjusted batching thresholds; final runs show neutral impact on long-seq workloads.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for serializer and kv_cache sharding. Integration tests exercise the pinned thread pool in a simulated NUMA environment. End-to-end canary run with continuous batching enabled and traffic shaping used to validate tail behavior. Stress tests for cache contention included.
